research_rationale:
Executive Order 11545 of July 9, 1970 (35 FR 11161) established the Defense Distinguished Service Medal under the President's authority as Commander in Chief; it rests on no statute, has no own-terms end, and sets no deadline, sunset or condition. The held original (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11545.txt, an official Federal Register text) contains four numbered sections and no other operative paragraph. The one held later instrument that names it is Executive Order 14085 of October 3, 2022 (87 FR 60541), section 6, which amends sections 1 and 2 by strike-and-insert and leaves sections 3 and 4 untouched; under the strike-and-insert ruling of 2026-10-21 the amended clauses continue until the parent order ends. The current U.S. Code (10 U.S.C. 1125 note, "Ex. Ord. No. 11545. Defense Distinguished Service Medal") reproduces all four sections as amended by Executive Order 14085, which shows the order operative in its amended form in the edition current through 2026-10-09. Machine searches of the U.S. Code, the eCFR and the Federal Register disposition catalog (read for coverage) found no revocation, supersession or termination. The held OCR of section 4 of the original omits words (a line after "when so" is missing); the Code note supplies the full text, and the clause is judged on that complete text. Original not authenticated beyond the held Federal Register text; no page images were inspected, none being required for this source.
